blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Concrete Driveway Cost in Eltham in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete guide to concrete driveway pricing for Eltham homeowners, covering plain, exposed aggregate and coloured options with real 2026 cost breakdowns.
body: If you are a homeowner in Eltham looking to upgrade your driveway, understanding the true cost of concrete is essential before you commit. The price of a new concrete driveway in Eltham depends on several factors, including the size of your driveway, the type of finish you choose, site access and any excavation or earthworks required. In Melbourne's north-east, where many properties feature sloped frontages and mature trees, site preparation can be a significant part of the overall cost. This guide breaks down the real numbers for Eltham homeowners in 2026 so you can plan your project with confidence.

For a standard plain concrete driveway in Eltham, you can expect to pay between $50 and $75 per square metre for a basic broom finish. A typical residential driveway of around 50 square metres would therefore cost approximately $2,500 to $3,750 for the concrete alone. However, this does not include excavation, base preparation, reinforcement or site grading, which can add $1,000 to $3,000 depending on your Eltham block. If your property sits on a slope or has tree roots near the driveway alignment, excavation costs will be higher. Always request an itemised quote that separates materials, labour and site works so you can compare offers accurately.

Exposed aggregate concrete is the most popular driveway choice in Eltham, and for good reason. It offers a premium, textured finish that complements the suburb's leafy, natural character. Expect to pay between $70 and $100 per square metre for exposed aggregate, bringing a typical 50 square metre driveway to $3,500 to $5,000 before site preparation. Coloured concrete sits in a similar range at $65 to $90 per square metre, while stamped or stencilled patterns can push costs to $100 to $150 per square metre. For Eltham homeowners wanting the best balance of durability and aesthetics, exposed aggregate remains the sweet spot between value and visual appeal.

Site preparation is where many Eltham driveway projects encounter unexpected costs. The suburb's clay soils expand and contract with Melbourne's seasonal rainfall, meaning proper base preparation is critical to prevent cracking and movement. A quality concrete contractor will excavate at least 150 millimetres, lay a compacted road base of crushed rock, install steel reinforcement or fibreglass mesh, and ensure adequate drainage. In Eltham, where many properties have established gardens and large gum trees near the driveway, root removal and root barriers may also be necessary. Skipping these steps to save money will almost certainly result in costly repairs within a few years.

The best time to pour a concrete driveway in Melbourne's north-east is during the drier months between October and April. Winter pours are possible but carry higher risk of frost damage and slower curing, particularly in Eltham where overnight temperatures can drop below freezing in July and August. If you are planning a driveway project, book your contractor in early spring to secure a spot before the busy season hits. Most reputable Eltham concreters, including Driveways, can provide a fixed-price quote weeks in advance, giving you time to budget and prepare your property before work begins.

When comparing quotes for your Eltham driveway, look beyond the headline price. Ask each contractor whether excavation, base preparation, reinforcement, curing and cleanup are included. A cheap quote that skimps on base preparation will cost you more in the long run. Check that your contractor is fully licensed and insured, and ask for examples of recent driveway work in Eltham or nearby suburbs like Greensborough and Research. At Driveways, we have been pouring driveways across Eltham for over 25 years, and every quote we provide is fixed, transparent and includes all site works. Call us today for a free on-site assessment.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete in Melbourne's North-East: A Seasonal Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: A practical seasonal guide for Eltham homeowners planning concrete projects, covering how Melbourne's climate affects curing, cracking and project timing.
body: Melbourne's unpredictable weather is the single biggest challenge for any concrete project, and Eltham is no exception. Located in Melbourne's north-east, Eltham experiences cool, wet winters and warm, dry summers, with rainfall fairly evenly distributed throughout the year. Pouring concrete in the wrong conditions can lead to cracking, surface scaling and poor curing, costing you thousands in repairs. This seasonal guide helps Eltham homeowners understand when conditions are ideal for a concrete pour, and when it is better to wait. Timing your project correctly is one of the simplest ways to ensure your concrete lasts for decades.

Spring, from September to November, is widely considered the best time to pour concrete in Eltham and across Melbourne's north-east. Daytime temperatures sit between 15 and 25 degrees Celsius, which is ideal for concrete curing. The ground has dried out after winter, reducing the risk of moisture-related issues, and there is usually enough dry weather to allow proper curing without the extreme heat of mid-summer. If you are planning a driveway, patio or slab project in Eltham, booking your contractor for early spring gives you the best conditions and avoids the rush that hits once the warmer weather arrives.

Summer concrete pours in Eltham come with their own set of challenges. While the dry weather is ideal, temperatures above 35 degrees Celsius can cause the surface moisture to evaporate too quickly, leading to surface cracking and a weak finish. In a typical Eltham summer, you will get several days over 30 degrees, and occasionally a run of extreme heat. Professional concreters manage this by scheduling early morning pours, using curing compounds and keeping the concrete wet for several days after placement. If you are planning a summer pour in Eltham, make sure your contractor has a heat management plan in place.

Winter concrete pours in Eltham require extra care but are certainly not impossible. Melbourne's north-east can experience overnight frosts from June through August, and Eltham's slightly elevated position means temperatures can be a few degrees cooler than the CBD. Concrete should not be poured when the ground is frozen or when temperatures are expected to drop below 5 degrees within 24 hours of placement. If conditions are suitable, a winter pour can actually benefit from slower curing, which can improve long-term strength. However, the risk of frost damage means most Eltham concreters recommend spring or autumn pours for critical projects.

Autumn, from March to May, is the second-best window for concrete pouring in Eltham. Temperatures are still mild, the summer heat has subsided and there is usually enough dry weather to complete most residential projects. Many Eltham homeowners schedule their driveway and patio projects for autumn, taking advantage of the comfortable working conditions and the fact that contractors are often less busy than in spring. One advantage of an autumn pour is that your concrete will have several months to cure before the heavier rainfall of winter arrives, giving it maximum strength before its first wet season in Eltham.

The most important takeaway for any Eltham concrete project is to work with a contractor who understands local conditions. A good concreter will monitor the weather forecast, adjust their pour schedule if needed and use the right admixtures and curing methods for the season. At Driveways, we have been pouring concrete across Eltham and Melbourne's north-east for over 25 years, and we know exactly how to get a great finish in any season. Whether you need a new driveway in spring or a shed slab in autumn, we will make sure the timing and conditions are right for a lasting result.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate vs Plain Concrete for Your Eltham Home
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed comparison of exposed aggregate and plain concrete for Eltham driveways, covering cost, durability, maintenance and which suits your property best.
body: Choosing between exposed aggregate and plain concrete is one of the most common decisions Eltham homeowners face when planning a new driveway, path or patio. Both options are durable, Australian-made and suitable for Melbourne's climate, but they look very different and come with different price points. Exposed aggregate has become the default choice in leafy suburbs like Eltham, where its natural, textured finish complements the area's bush setting and established gardens. Plain concrete, on the other hand, offers a clean, minimalist look at a lower cost. In this guide, we compare both options across the factors that matter most to Eltham homeowners.

Plain concrete, also called a broom or trowel finish, is the most affordable option for driveways and slabs in Eltham. It delivers a clean, uniform surface that works well with modern and contemporary home designs. The main advantage of plain concrete is its simplicity and lower price point, typically costing $50 to $75 per square metre compared to $70 to $100 for exposed aggregate. However, plain concrete shows stains, tyre marks and surface wear more visibly than textured alternatives. In Eltham, where leaf litter and tree sap are common due to the suburb's mature vegetation, plain concrete driveways may require more frequent cleaning to maintain their appearance.

Exposed aggregate is created by washing away the top layer of cement paste to reveal the decorative stones underneath. The result is a slip-resistant, visually rich surface that hides dirt and wear far better than plain concrete. Eltham homeowners love exposed aggregate because it suits the suburb's natural landscape, blending beautifully with established gardens and native plantings. You can choose from hundreds of stone and colour combinations, from classic river pebbles to modern black and charcoal blends. The textured surface also provides excellent grip underfoot, making it a practical choice for Eltham's sloped driveways and pathways where safety is a concern.

When it comes to long-term maintenance, exposed aggregate has a clear advantage for Eltham properties. The textured surface naturally conceals minor stains, tyre marks and weathering, meaning it stays looking good with minimal effort. A simple pressure wash once or twice a year is usually all that is needed to keep an exposed aggregate driveway in top condition. Plain concrete, by contrast, tends to show every oil drip, leaf stain and surface blemish. For busy Eltham families and property investors, the lower maintenance requirements of exposed aggregate often outweigh the higher upfront cost, making it the better value over the full life of the driveway.

In terms of durability, both exposed aggregate and plain concrete perform well in Melbourne's climate when properly installed. The key difference is that exposed aggregate's textured surface is more forgiving of minor surface movement and wear, while plain concrete can develop visible hairline cracks more readily. In Eltham, where clay soils expand and contract with seasonal moisture changes, this resilience is a significant advantage. A properly prepared base with adequate reinforcement is essential for both finishes, but exposed aggregate's ability to mask minor imperfections makes it a more forgiving choice for Eltham's variable soil conditions. Both options will last 25 years or more with correct installation.

For most Eltham homeowners, exposed aggregate is the recommended choice for driveways and high-traffic outdoor areas. Its combination of aesthetics, durability and low maintenance makes it ideal for the suburb's leafy, family-friendly character. Plain concrete remains a solid option for shed slabs, utility areas and budget-conscious projects where appearance is less critical. At Driveways, we pour both finishes regularly across Eltham and can show you sample boards and completed projects in your area. With over 25 years of experience in Melbourne's north-east, we will help you choose the right concrete finish for your home and budget. Call us for a free quote today.

blogPosts.title: Retaining Walls in Eltham: Materials, Costs and Melbourne Council Rules
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything Eltham homeowners need to know about retaining walls, from material choices and pricing to Nillumbik Shire council permit requirements.
body: Eltham's hilly terrain and undulating blocks make retaining walls a common necessity for homeowners looking to create usable outdoor space. Whether you need to hold back a sloped backyard, create a level area for a shed or manage stormwater runoff, a properly engineered retaining wall is essential. In Melbourne's north-east, where many properties feature significant fall across the block, retaining walls are not just a landscaping choice but a structural requirement. This guide covers the main retaining wall materials available to Eltham homeowners, the approximate costs involved and the council regulations you need to know before building any wall on your property.

Concrete sleeper retaining walls are the most popular choice in Eltham and across Melbourne's north-east. They offer excellent strength, a clean modern look and a lifespan of 50 years or more. Concrete sleepers are installed on galvanised steel posts set into the ground, creating a rigid wall that can handle significant soil pressure. For a standard 600 millimetre high concrete sleeper wall in Eltham, expect to pay between $150 and $250 per linear metre, fully installed. Taller walls over one metre require engineering certification under Melbourne's building regulations, which adds to the overall cost but ensures your wall is safe and compliant with Australian Standards.

Timber retaining walls offer a more natural, organic look that suits many Eltham properties, particularly those with established gardens and native plantings. Treated pine sleepers are the most common timber option, costing between $100 and $180 per linear metre for a standard height wall. While timber is cheaper upfront than concrete, it has a shorter lifespan of 15 to 25 years and is susceptible to termites, rot and weathering in Melbourne's variable climate. For Eltham homeowners choosing timber, ensure the sleepers are H4 treated for ground contact and that adequate drainage is installed behind the wall to prevent premature deterioration of the timber structure.

Block and stone retaining walls provide a premium, architecturally striking option for Eltham homes. Constructed from interlocking concrete blocks or natural stone, these walls can be dry-stacked or mortared depending on the height and engineering requirements. Costs range from $200 to $400 per linear metre for block walls, and $300 to $600 for natural stone. In Eltham, where many homes have a contemporary or mid-century aesthetic, block walls in charcoal or earth tones are increasingly popular. These walls require a solid concrete footing and professional installation to ensure they meet Melbourne's building code requirements for structural retaining walls on residential properties.

In Melbourne, any retaining wall over 600 millimetres in height requires a building permit and must be designed by a qualified engineer. This is especially important in Eltham, where the combination of clay soils, sloped blocks and mature tree roots creates complex engineering conditions. The Nillumbik Shire Council requires plans to be submitted through a private building surveyor, and inspections may be required during construction. Drainage behind the retaining wall is critical in Eltham's clay soil environment, as trapped water creates enormous hydrostatic pressure that can cause wall failure. A professional installer will always include agricultural drain pipe and gravel backfill behind any retaining wall.

When planning a retaining wall project in Eltham, always engage a contractor who understands local soil conditions and council requirements. Ask for evidence of engineering certification, previous work in the area and confirmation that all necessary permits will be obtained before construction begins. With over 25 years of experience building on Eltham's challenging terrain, we know what it takes to build a retaining wall that will stand strong for decades.
